items.title: S&P 500 e Nasdaq fecham em baixa por ações do setor de tecnologia; investidores avaliams medidas sobre Irã
items.author: Saeed Azhar, Purvi Agarwal, Niket Nishant
items.creator: Saeed Azhar, Purvi Agarwal, Niket Nishant
items.summary: O S&P 500 e o Nasdaq encerraram em baixa nesta segunda-feira, prejudicados pelas ações do setor de tecnologia, enquanto os investidores avaliavam as novas pressões econômicas dos EUA contra o Irã e se preparavam para uma semana que inclui a divulgação dos resultados da Nvidia e um relatório sobre a inflação que será acompanhado de perto.
items.body:
O S&P 500 e o Nasdaq encerraram em baixa nesta segunda-feira, prejudicados pelas ações do setor de tecnologia, enquanto os investidores avaliavam as novas pressões econômicas dos EUA contra o Irã e se preparavam para uma semana que inclui a divulgação dos resultados da Nvidia e um relatório sobre a inflação que será acompanhado de perto.
O governo Trump anunciou nesta segunda-feira uma possível ampliação das sanções contra países que mantêm relações comerciais com o Irã, como parte do que chamou de “Dia D econômico”, mas não chegou a impor penalidades de fato.
As ações do setor de chips sofreram forte correção, arrastando para baixo o índice Philadelphia SE Semiconductor (.SOX) . A Nvidia (NVDA.O) caiu 2,9%, a Micron Technology (MU.O) tombou 5,8% e a Broadcom (AVGO.O) registrou queda de 2,6%, pressionando o índice de Tecnologia da Informação do S&P 500 (.SPLRCT) .
O otimismo em relação às empresas de tecnologia também foi afetado pela crescente oposição política aos data centers de IA.
O governador do Texas, Greg Abbott, fez uma das advertências mais contundentes já feitas por um republicano ao setor de IA, afirmando que as empresas de data centers “cavaram sua própria cova” e merecem a reação negativa que estão enfrentando por não terem conseguido o apoio da comunidade, informou o Axios no domingo.
Neste mês, Abbott ordenou uma pausa nas aprovações de novos projetos de data centers por meio do processo estadual de interconexão à rede elétrica, citando preocupações de que um aumento na demanda por eletricidade pudesse ameaçar a confiabilidade do sistema, em um momento em que a oposição aos projetos está crescendo.
“A maior preocupação que temos é a retórica agressiva que estamos começando a ouvir de políticos sobre IA e data centers”, disse Ohsung Kwon, estrategista-chefe de ações do Wells Fargo. “Temos destacado isso como um grande risco à medida que nos aproximamos das eleições de meio de mandato.”
No entanto, o setor financeiro (.SPSY) registrou alta, com o JPMorgan Chase (JPM.N) subindo 1,4% e a Visa (V.N) subindo 3%. Essas empresas também mantiveram o índice Dow Jones de blue-chip em alta.
O Índice Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) subiu 0,26%, para 53.417,16 pontos, o S&P 500 (.SPX) caiu 0,28%, para 7.652,86 pontos, e o Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) recuou 0,76%, para 25.980,19 pontos.
ATENÇÃO VOLTADA PARA O DISCURSO DE WARSH EM JACKSON HOLE Preocupações com o aumento vertiginoso da dívida pública levaram o rendimento dos títulos de 30 anos ao nível mais alto em 19 anos antes de o Tesouro anunciar medidas de apoio na semana passada.
A CNBC informou nesta segunda-feira que o secretário do Tesouro, Scott Bessent, poderia recorrer à Conta Geral do departamento, de quase US$1 trilhão, para ajudar a financiar a recompra de títulos. No entanto, o rendimento dos títulos do Tesouro dos EUA de 30 anos permaneceu acima de 5%.
Essa turbulência intensificou o foco no discurso do chair do Federal Reserve, Kevin Warsh, no simpósio de Jackson Hole na sexta-feira, onde os investidores buscarão pistas sobre a interpretação dos formuladores de políticas em relação aos esforços de resgate do Tesouro.
Os resultados trimestrais da gigante de IA Nvidia devem ser outro catalisador importante para os mercados. Qualquer sinal de desaceleração no crescimento poderia reacender as preocupações com as valorizações exageradas.
“A Nvidia precisa impressionar para manter um dos pilares do mercado de ações estável, e Warsh precisa trazer clareza sobre as taxas de juros para manter o outro pilar estável”, disse Richard Reyle, diretor de investimentos da Questar Capital Partners.
Os mercados também acompanharão o relatório de Gastos com Consumo Pessoal (PCE), o indicador de inflação preferido do Fed, com divulgação prevista para quarta-feira. Isso se dará após um relatório de inflação ao consumidor favorável divulgado neste mês, que reduziu as chances de um aumento imediato nas taxas de juros.
Os operadores esperam um aumento de 25 pontos-base até o final de 2026, de acordo com dados da LSEG.
Separadamente, o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, alertou que as tarifas sobre carros, caminhões e peças automotivas do Canadá seriam aumentadas para 50% a partir de 1º de janeiro, após o fracasso das negociações comerciais no fim de semana.
As montadoras Ford (F.N) e General Motors (GM.N) caíram 3,3% e 1,1%, respectivamente, enquanto a empresa de transporte rodoviário J.B. Hunt Transport (JBHT.O) registrou queda de cerca de 5,7%.

items.title: Vídeo de Brizola criticando Bolsonaro é montagem
items.author: Reuters Fact Check
items.creator: Reuters Fact Check
items.summary: Um vídeo em que Leonel Brizola, ex-governador do Rio Grande do Sul e do Rio de Janeiro, critica o ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro é uma versão adulterada de uma participação do político gaúcho em um debate presidencial em 1989.
items.body:
Um vídeo em que Leonel Brizola, ex-governador do Rio Grande do Sul e do Rio de Janeiro, critica o ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro é uma versão adulterada de uma participação do político gaúcho em um debate presidencial em 1989.
Aqui estão os principais detalhes:
Posts mostram um vídeo em que Brizola acusa Bolsonaro de mandar em milícias e afirma que ele é “o único bandido corrupto que seus eleitores consideram honesto”.
“Em 1989, Brizola já alertava sobre Bolsonaro”, diz a legenda da publicação.
A gravação original é da participação de Brizola no debate do SBT no primeiro turno da eleição presidencial de 1989. O político não mencionou o ex-presidente em nenhum momento do programa.
Em 1989, Bolsonaro era vereador no Rio de Janeiro, conforme sua biografia no site da Câmara dos Deputados.
Veredicto: Alterado digitalmente. O vídeo original é um trecho de um debate presidencial em que Brizola não citou Bolsonaro.

items.title: WikiHow sues OpenAI for copyright infringement over AI training
items.author: Blake Brittain
items.creator: Blake Brittain
items.summary: Do-it-yourself website WikiHow sued OpenAI in Manhattan federal court for allegedly misusing its instructional material to train its popular chatbot ChatGPT.
items.body:
Do-it-yourself website WikiHow sued OpenAI in Manhattan federal court for allegedly misusing its instructional material to train its popular chatbot ChatGPT.
WikiHow's lawsuit , filed on Friday, said that the AI company scraped thousands of its how-to articles to help train ChatGPT to respond to human prompts.
The lawsuit is part of a wave of cases brought by publishers, authors and other copyright holders against AI companies over the alleged misuse of their material to train chatbots like ChatGPT, Anthropic's Claude, Meta's Llama and Google's Gemini.
An OpenAI spokesperson said on Monday that the company's AI models are "trained on publicly available data and grounded in fair use." Spokespeople and attorneys for wikiHow did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the new lawsuit on Monday.
WikiHow publishes instructional articles on "subjects ranging from routine tasks to specialized skills," the company said in its complaint. The lawsuit said that OpenAI scraped more than 11,000 of its articles without permission to train its GPT large language models.
WikiHow also said that ChatGPT reproduces its text in response to user prompts and threatens to displace its market.
"Having ingested wikiHow’s articles, those models now produce competing how-to content on the same subjects, at a fraction of the time, effort, and cost of researching, writing, and editing a wikiHow article," the lawsuit said. "The substitution cuts wikiHow’s revenue and, over time, its reason to keep producing the articles at all."
The lawsuit alleges OpenAI copied WikiHow's work "at scale" and infringed at least 1,200 of WikiHow's registered copyrights. WikiHow requested an unspecified amount of monetary damages and a court order blocking OpenAI from infringing its copyrights.
The case is WikiHow Inc v. OpenAI Inc, U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, No. 1:26-cv-07171.
For WikiHow: Rohit Nath and Alejandra Salinas of Susman Godfrey
For OpenAI: attorney information not yet available

FAST

NEW YORK, Aug 24 : The U.S. dollar advanced on Monday, coming off its third weekly decline in four that sent the greenback to three-month lows after President Donald Trump's administration announced an expansion of sanctions on Iran and separate tariffs on goods from Canada.
The greenback extended gains after U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced the expansion of secondary sanctions in hopes they will "sever every economic lifeline" that sustains Iran in the latest effort to pressure Tehran into ending its attacks on ships in the Gulf.
After last week's announcement by the Treasury Department that it would double the size of liquidity support buyback operations for longer-dated notes and bonds, CNBC reported earlier on Monday, citing two senior Treasury officials, that Bessent could tap the department's near $1 trillion General Account to help fund bond buybacks, instead of issuing short-term bills.
The dollar briefly pared some gains after the report, along with longer-dated Treasury yields.

"If the reporting is true that the Treasury is going to announce using a slug of its Treasury General Account at the Fed to buy longer-term bonds, it could be an interesting experiment. Does firing a bazooka at a hurricane work?" said Brian Jacobsen, chief economist at Annex Wealth Management in Menomonee Falls, Wisconsin.
"Lower bond yields at the long end won’t fix the debt problem. Longer term, it could make it worse. The government’s debt burden would become even more sensitive to changes in the Fed’s policy rate."
The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, rose 0.17 per cent to 98.99, with the euro down 0.14 per cent at $1.1663.
Long-end yields have been climbing around the globe due to a combination of a solid economic growth outlook, expectations for rising inflation and concern about swelling sovereign debts, while the Treasury buyback expansion to relieve upward pressure on yields has fueled concerns the dollar will weaken as a result.
CANADIAN DOLLAR WEAKENS ON TARIFFS
Trade tensions weighed on the Canadian dollar, which weakened 0.61 per cent, its biggest drop since June 17, versus the greenback to C$1.385 per dollar and was on track to snap a three-day streak of gains, after Washington imposed 50 per cent tariffs on Canadian goods, with Canada promising to retaliate "dollar for dollar" on the new levies.
Trump said in a social media post on Monday that the U.S. will increase tariffs to 50 per cent on all cars, trucks, automotive parts and steel from Canada starting January 1, 2027.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said a "mutually beneficial deal" with the U.S. was possible, but only if Americans respect Canada's sovereignty.
Sterling dipped 0.06 per cent to $1.3632, holding near its six-month high of $1.3675 hit on Friday. The Japanese yen softened 0.13 per cent against the greenback to 159.13 per dollar.
In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin gained 2.05 per cent to $78,993.42 after registering its largest weekly gain in nearly 3-1/2 years last week.
KEY DATA RELEASES, WARSH REMARKS EYED
U.S. economic data this week includes the personal consumption expenditures price index, personal income and spending, consumer confidence and the second estimate of second-quarter economic growth.
Market participants will also be hoping for some guidance on the outlook for U.S. interest rates when Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh speaks in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, on Friday.
However, UBS economists said in a note that Warsh's "quest to end any and all forms of forward guidance suggests we probably won't hear where the funds rate is headed," while Morgan Stanley's chief U.S. economist Michael Gapen said, "We expect silence on the near-term outlook for monetary policy, including the expansion of the Treasury buyback program."

items.title: Trump's approval holds at record low as US support for Iran war falls, Reuters Ipsos poll finds
items.author: Jason Lange
items.creator: Jason Lange
items.summary: A Reuters/Ipsos poll showed just 31% of Americans support U.S. military action against Iran, down from 37% in March, in a decline driven by fewer self-identified Republicans backing the conflict.
items.body:
U.S. public approval of the war with Iran fell to its lowest level since the conflict's early days, helping to hold President Donald Trump's popularity at a record low, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll that closed on Monday.
The four-day poll showed just 31% of Americans support U.S. military action against Iran, down from 37% in a March Reuters/Ipsos poll and 34% earlier this month. The decline was driven by fewer self-identified Republicans backing the conflict. Some 69% of Republican respondents support the war, compared with 77% in March.
The war has been dragging on Trump's public standing this year, and for the second survey in a row just 33% of respondents said they approved of the Republican's performance in the White House, the lowest level in Reuters/Ipsos polls in Trump's first or second term.
Trump has told Americans that the war - which started with U.S.-Israeli attacks on Iran on February 28 - is necessary to keep Tehran from developing a nuclear weapon. The conflict has cooled in recent months but Iran has kept in place a de facto blockade of oil exports from the region, which has pushed U.S. gasoline prices near record highs.
Trump has vowed to ramp up economic pressure on Iran and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Monday announced a possible expansion of sanctions on countries doing business with the country, but stopped short of actually imposing penalties, a sign of how thorny the conflict has become for the administration.
FEARS OF A LONG WAR Some 83% of the country thinks the war will go on "for an extended period of time," the latest Reuters/Ipsos poll found, up from 80% earlier this month.
Trump campaigned ahead of the 2024 presidential election on promises to control inflation and avoid lengthy military conflicts. Six months into the war with Iran, U.S. gasoline prices are more than a dollar higher per gallon than they were before the war. That is weighing on Trump's Republican allies who will be defending narrow congressional majorities in the November 3 midterm elections.
Independent voters in the poll favored Democrats over Republicans - 33% to 19% - when asked who they would vote for in congressional elections if the election were held today.
The poll surveyed 1,215 U.S. adults nationwide and had a margin of error of 3 percentage points in either direction.

US widens sanctions on Iran but withholds more punishing options

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Washington would be working with US partners to target any source of Iran's "illicit revenue".

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent speaks during a press conference to outline further sanctions against Iran, at the Treasury Department in Washington, DC, US, Aug 24, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Evelyn Hockstein)

FAST

WASHINGTON: The US on Monday (Aug 24) unveiled an expansion of sanctions that it said would cut off Iran's economic lifeline but stopped short of the most punishing measures, instead putting the world on notice to cease doing business with the Islamic Republic.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said other countries would need to sever business ties with Iran or risk being forced out of the dollar-based financial system.
But he declined to identify the countries that would be targeted or reveal when those penalties would take effect, saying he would instead provide them time to comply with the new directive.
"We are giving everyone the opportunity to remedy bad behaviour. Why would I want to blow up the global financial system?" Bessent said at a news conference.

The Treasury Department did announce new sanctions on 60 individuals, entities and vessels, but the list did not include any of the Chinese financial institutions suspected of facilitating Iran's oil trade.
Struggling to resolve an unpopular war that has pushed energy prices higher, Washington appears to be counting on further economic pressure even though Iran has spent decades under layers of US and international sanctions that have battered its economy but have not deterred its leadership.
Though neither side has launched major strikes in weeks, the war shows little sign of reaching a diplomatic solution. In the meantime, the US is seeking new ways to end Iranian attacks on ships in the Gulf and, more recently, via its allies in the Red Sea.

Related:

Iran says new sanctions threatened by 'desperate' US will fail

Iran says it finds new gas, after war hits energy sector

Before the announcement, Iran threatened both a possible military response and further reduction in oil exports from the Gulf in response to any US economic measures. Afterwards, Iranian Economy Minister Ali Madanizadeh said, "We are fully prepared for the US sanctions."
"Naturally, the enemies intend to launch an economic terrorist attack on us, but we also have our own tools and know how to play the game. Our defence is no longer so defensive; the enemies should wait for an attack," Madanizadeh told state television.
Brigadier General Hossein Mohebbi, a spokesperson for Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, vowed heavy blows to US vital interests and energy chokepoints if Iran's infrastructure is threatened, Press TV reported.
Almost six months have passed since the US and Israel launched strikes on Iran, sparking a conflict that has snarled shipping in the region, reduced the flow of oil and taken a toll on the US and global economies. Thousands of people have died, most of them in Iran and Lebanon.
While the war has degraded much of Iran's conventional military capacity, inflicted economic pain and killed then-Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, Iran has preserved enough missile and drone capability to attack its Gulf neighbours and threaten oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, bringing shipping in the key waterway to a near standstill. 
The exact state of Iran's nuclear program, which the Americans and Israelis aim to wipe out, remains unknown.
Oil prices fell more than US$2 a barrel on Monday, though investors braced for the prospect of further supply disruptions from the Middle East.

Related:

Oil prices fall as Bessent outlines new steps to punish Iran

"NO ONE" BEYOND REACH OF SANCTIONS Madanizadeh, the economy minister, said neither China nor Russia had "accepted" the US measures, and predicted other countries would resist them.
Bessent previously urged cooperation from China, the biggest buyer of Iranian oil for several years, although the US blockade of Iran's ports, renewed in mid-July, has already cut Iranian oil flows to China.
Experts say Washington is wary of Chinese retaliation for any sanctions on its banks ahead of expected talks next month between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, with any curbs on China's exports of critical minerals especially sensitive.
Asked about Chinese banks on Monday, Bessent said, "We want to make clear here today that no one is above the reach of US sanctions."
The Chinese Foreign Ministry said sanctions and pressure tactics do not help and Beijing would do what was necessary to protect China's interests.
Bessent said the Treasury Department has mapped the networks, facilitators and financial channels that Iran uses to smuggle oil and evade sanctions. He said Washington would be working with US partners to target any source of Iran's "illicit revenue".
The department said the Iranian government was using five sectors - digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping - to prop up its economy, and they were on notice for sanctions.
Earlier on Monday, Iran issued a new warning to shipping not to pass through the Strait of Hormuz without its permission, listing 45 ships it said had violated its rules and threatening retaliation for any ship-to-ship transfers with them.

items.title: Law firm Paul Weiss taps new Supreme Court practice head after Shanmugam exit
items.author: Sara Merken
items.creator: Sara Merken
items.summary: Law firm Paul Weiss has hired William Jay to lead its Supreme Court and appellate litigation practice, filling the role after the group's prominent head Kannon Shanmugam left for another firm earlier this year.
items.body:
Law firm Paul Weiss has hired William Jay to lead its Supreme Court and appellate litigation practice, filling the role after the group's prominent head Kannon Shanmugam left for another firm earlier this year.
Jay, who has argued 19 cases before the U.S. Supreme Court, joins Paul Weiss as a Washington, D.C.-based partner, the firm said on Monday. He has represented clients including Teva Pharmaceuticals, Varsity Brands and B&B Hardware.
Shanmugam, who previously led the Supreme Court practice at Paul Weiss, [USN:L6N4161HM TEXT:"departed"] with Masha Hansford in April to launch a new practice at law firm Davis Polk.
Jay practiced at Goodwin for 14 years. He previously worked as an assistant to the Solicitor General. Earlier in his career he was a clerk to former U.S. Supreme Court Justice Antonin Scalia.
Jay told Reuters that he was eager to join Paul Weiss as the New York firm grows its litigation department.
Paul Weiss has hired a handful of litigation partners this year, including former U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission deputy enforcement director Antonia Apps in February. The firm has also seen litigator departures, including a pair of partners who joined Linklaters in July.

items.title: Hyundai Motor's union reaches tentative wage deal, averting more strikes
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Hyundai Motor's South Korean union said on Tuesday it has reached a tentative agreement with management, averting further production losses after staging its first full strike in a decade on Friday, following a series of partial stoppages.
items.body:
Hyundai Motor's (005380.KS) South Korean union said on Tuesday it has reached a tentative agreement with management, averting further production losses after staging its first full strike in a decade on Friday, following a series of partial stoppages.
The union had demanded higher bonuses, an increase in the retirement age, and job protections against artificial intelligence and automation.
The tentative agreement includes a base salary increase of 100,000 won ($72.31) per month plus a performance bonus equivalent to 400% of base pay and additional payouts in cash and bonuses.
The retirement age will be extended from the current 60 upon amendment of a relevant law, without reducing salary for the first few years after 60, the union said.
From next year until 2028, 500 new technical workers will be hired.
Hyundai Motor did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment outside regular business hours.
The union had demanded the company set aside 30% of net income for bonuses and guarantee job security, raising concerns over the growing adoption of robotics and artificial intelligence on assembly lines.
Regarding union demands on job security related to AI, the two sides agreed to discuss matters related to employment when it comes to rolling out new businesses, according to the agreement seen by Reuters.
Hyundai, which owns humanoid robot maker Boston Dynamics, has said it plans to deploy humanoid robots at its U.S. plant in Georgia from 2028, with the aim of expanding their use across its production sites.
($1 = 1,382.8900 won)

items.title: Gold price rises, silver slips on Treasury cash-pile buyback signal
items.author: Scott Spence
items.creator: Scott Spence
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent could tap a $935 billion cash pile to fund bond buybacks.
items.body:
Gold price rises, silver slips on Treasury cash-pile buyback signal

Scott Spence | August 24, 2026 | 10:50 am
Markets   USA   Gold   Silver  

Stock image.

Gold rose while silver slipped on Monday after CNBC reported that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent could tap a $935 billion cash pile to fund bond buybacks, pushing long-term yields lower.

The department could draw on the Treasury General Account to fund buybacks of higher-yielding older securities, CNBC reported Monday, citing two senior Treasury officials.

The TGA, essentially the government’s checking account at the Federal Reserve, stood at $935 billion as of Aug. 20. Bessent called the operation a “Treasury Twist” in a CNBC interview, a reference to buying long-term bonds funded by short-term issuance.

The officials would not say how much, if any, of the TGA would be used. The report follows Bessent’s decision last week to double buybacks on the long end from $2 billion to at least $4 billion. Gold climbed 1.2% as of 12.30pm in New York, near a four-month high around $4,719 an ounce.

The 10-year Treasury yield fell as much as four basis points to 4.69%, and the all-important 30- year dropped to around 5.215%. Yields are slightly lower, however they remain near the levels that prompted the Treasury to intervene last week, when the 30-year touched a 19-year high above 5.27%.

Silver is down around 1% on the day, as price consolidates below the $70 resistance level. Silver has outrun gold in August, up almost 20% on the month vs gold’s 15%.

Copper gained a modest 0.46% and trades just below its all-time highs.

Another Band-aid

Monday’s Treasury move drew skepticism from Blake Gwinn, head of US rate strategy at RBC< Capital Markets, who called it “a very slapdash attempt to try to stem the selloff” and put the odds of the department actually using the cash at “very, very low,” Bloomberg reported.

The Treasury expanded its buyback program last week after long-dated yields hit multi-year highs, a move that provided only temporary relief as the 30-year yield erased the gains within a day. The week ahead will test investors, the Fed and the Treasury.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivers his first Jackson Hole speech Friday, and July PCE data lands Wednesday, with economists surveyed by Bloomberg forecasting about 3.6% headline and 3.3% core year-over-year.

The Treasury will have it’s eyes firmly glued to long term rates.

(With files from Bloomberg)

items.title: 米国が新たな対イラン制裁、取引続ける国も対象－「経済版Dデー」
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： ベッセント米財務長官は24日、イランを世界経済から孤立させ6カ月近くに及ぶ戦争を終結させるため自ら「経済版Dデー」と呼ぶ作戦の一環として、イランと取引するあらゆる国に経済的な制裁を科すと警告した。

ベッセント氏はワシントンで開いた記者会見で、「われわれは世界各地に広がるイランの金融ネットワークに対し、経済的な猛攻撃を開始する」と表明。「イラン政権を経済的に窒息させるものだ」とし、イラン資金の洗浄に関与する場合、ドルへのアクセスを遮断すると述べた。

また、トランプ米大統領が各国首脳に電話し、「イラン政権との関係を停止するよう具体的に要請している」とも説明。各国にはイランとの関係を打ち切るための明確な期限が設定されており、従わなければ米財務省が単独で措置を講じる考えを示した。

今回の表明は、イランに屈服を迫る米国の最新の試みとなる。イランは数十年にわたり経済制裁を受け、2月下旬に始まった米国による爆撃が数カ月続いているにもかかわらず、米国の要求を拒み続けている。また、11月の中間選挙が近づく中、米国民の間で極めて不人気な戦争を終わらせようとするトランプ氏の焦りが強まっていることも浮き彫りになった。

今回の措置によってイランが世界経済や一部の貿易相手国からさらに孤立する可能性はあるが、イランに米国の要求を受け入れさせ、ホルムズ海峡の開放につなげられるかは不透明だ。

ベッセント氏の警告は、米国を中国との対立に向かわせるリスクもある。中国はイラン産原油の大半を購入しており、これまで購入停止を拒んできた。ベッセント氏は、イランの貿易相手国に直ちに制裁を科さない理由を問われると、こうした措置のリスクを認めた。

同氏は「われわれは全ての国に、不適切な行動を改める機会を与えている」と説明。「私が世界の金融システムを破壊したいと思うだろうか」と付け加えた。

米財務省は24日、60を超える団体への制裁を発表した。ベッセント氏は、イランにとって「最も重要な5つの生命線」に照準を合わせていると説明し、デジタル資産、テクノロジー、金、航空、海運を挙げた。さらに、イランとの関係を巡り、今週末までに大手金融機関1社を制裁対象にすると警告したが、対象の名前は明らかにしなかった。

items.title: 【欧州市況】長期債買われる、米国債高が下支え－株は方向感欠く展開
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 24日の欧州債券市場は、米国債の上昇が支えとなり、長期債が小幅上昇した。欧州中央銀行（ECB）が年末までに2回利上げするとの観測が強まったことから、短期債は下落した。

ドイツ30年債利回りは1ベーシスポイント（bp、1bp＝0.01%）低下して3.76%となった。英30年債利回りも2bp低下し、5.79%となった。世界の長期国債は財政懸念の強まりを背景に、売り圧力にさらされている。米30年債利回りは24日に低下しているものの、引き続き2007年以来の高水準近くにある。

ドイツ2年債利回りは3bp上昇して2.86%だった。短期債が相対的に軟調だったため、イールドカーブはツイスト・フラット化した。短期金融市場は、ECBの年末までの利上げ幅を計45bpと織り込んでいる。見通しは21日時点から小幅に拡大した。

フランスでは、新年度予算編成に向けた財政懸念と政治リスクが重しとなり、10年債利回りが2008年終盤以来の高水準近くにとどまっている。フランス10年債とドイツ10年債の利回り差（スプレッド）は87bp前後となっている。

欧州株は薄商いの中、ほぼ横ばいだった。ストックス欧州600指数はほぼ変わらずで取引を終えた。旅行・娯楽セクターが最も高いパフォーマンスとなり、原油価格の下落を受けて、航空株が上昇した。

欧州株は好調な決算発表シーズンが終了して以降、方向感を欠いている。投資家は新たな相場材料を求め、フランスのインフレ統計や米国で今週開かれるジャクソンホール会合（カンザスシティー連銀主催の年次シンポジウム）など、経済指標や中央銀行関連のイベントに注目している。

WASHINGTON, Aug 24 : U.S. President Donald Trump invested as much as $50,000 in Elon Musk's SpaceX in June, according to a public financial disclosure, giving him a financial stake in a major government contractor run by his former adviser. 
He bought between $15,001 and $50,000 in shares on June 23, according to a financial disclosure signed by him on August 12 and made public on August 22. The purchase was part of more than 1,000 stock trades the president made in June.
SpaceX priced the biggest-ever U.S. IPO on June 12, valuing the space, satellite and AI provider at $1.77 trillion.
In a statement to Reuters, White House spokesman Davis Ingle said that third-party financial institutions independently manage the president's portfolio and replicate "recognized indexes, such as the Schwab 1000."

"Neither President Trump nor any member of his family has any ability to direct, influence or provide input regarding how the portfolio is invested or when investments are bought or sold," Ingle said in the statement. 
Trump's investment in SpaceX adds a new financial link between the president and Musk's rocket company at a time when the administration is making decisions that could affect the firm's fortunes. 
SpaceX is a U.S. military contractor, and often seeks approvals from federal agencies. Trump on Thursday directed his team to help drastically increase the number of U.S. commercial space launches. SpaceX is a dominant player in that sector. 
U.S. Small Business Administration leader and Trump cabinet member Kelly Loeffler earned millions from SpaceX's IPO, Reuters previously reported. Loeffler first invested in xAI, Musk’s AI and social media firm that has since merged with SpaceX. She invested again after Trump nominated her to lead the SBA. 
Her first investment in xAI would have been worth between $7 million and $2.6 billion on the day of the IPO, depending on the exact amount she invested and the date she made it, said Franco Granda, analyst at data provider PitchBook. The second investment would have been worth between $2.2 million and $25.4 million that day, he said.
Reuters could not immediately determine the precise amount of Trump's investment because federal officials use ranges to declare the value of their assets on their financial disclosure forms.

UK, Ukraine sign AI defence partnership linked to battlefield technology

The deal will focus on AI-enabled battlefield sensors, low-power chips for drones, and other defence technologies.

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham delivers a speech next to Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy during the Coalition of the Willing meeting, in Kyiv, Ukraine Aug 24, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Henry Nicholls)

FAST

LONDON: Britain said on Monday (Aug 24) it had signed a partnership with Ukraine to jointly develop artificial intelligence tools for defence and security, giving British researchers access to a Ukrainian battlefield data platform used to train military AI systems.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham and President Volodymyr Zelenskyy signed the agreement in Kyiv, making Britain the first international partner to access Ukraine's Avengers AI Labs, a government statement said.
Avengers Labs was built around an annotated dataset of 5 million battlefield images, Ukraine's Defence Ministry said earlier in August, largely drawn from the military's DELTA combat system - a domestically developed battlefield management and situational-awareness system.
The platform uses data collected from cameras and sensors across Ukraine's battlefield, including information on tanks, artillery systems, drones and other military targets.

The Ukrainian ministry said AI models trained on the data were already being used in an automated target-detection system that analyses more than 100,000 drone video feeds each month and can identify about 70 per cent of enemy targets in real time.
Under the deal, Britain and Ukraine will collaborate on pilot projects including technology that uses fibre-optic cables as AI-enabled sensors to help protect military facilities, and research into low-power AI chips for drones and autonomous systems.
The British government said the partnership would initially focus on defence and national security projects bringing together researchers, engineers, technology companies and military experts from both countries.
Burnham on Monday visited Ukraine for his first trip abroad since becoming prime minister, where he had talks with Zelenskyy and co-chaired a meeting of the "Coalition of the Willing."
His office had earlier announced Britain would allow missile maker MBDA to release classified information on British-made components used in the SCALP long-range cruise missile to help establish assembly lines in Ukraine.

China's Xi likely to visit India with big delegation for first time in seven years

India-China relations have remained strained for years, largely due to ongoing border tensions and territorial disputes.

Chinese President Xi Jinping and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi meet on the sidelines of the BRICS summit in Kazan, Russia, on Oct 23, 2024. (File photo: Reuters/China Daily)

FAST

NEW DELHI: Chinese President Xi Jinping is likely to attend next month's BRICS summit in New Delhi with a large delegation , three sources said, in what would be his first visit in seven years and a fresh sign of a thaw between the rivals.
India is hosting the Sep 12 to 13 summit, where Xi 's presence would be watched less for the BRICS agenda than for what it signals about Beijing and New Delhi's efforts to stabilise relations after deadly border clashes in 2020 .
"Chinese officials are busy finalising hotels and security protocols," one of the India n sources with direct knowledge told Reuters.
Last year, India n Prime Minister Narendra Modi visit ed China for the first time in seven years , but the relationship has only improved gradually. More recently, a fresh border-related dispute triggered sharp diplomatic exchanges between the two sides.

Two other India n sources said Xi was likely to be accompanied by a delegation of about 400 officials, compared with fewer than 200 officials the last time in 2019.
Officials from both countries are expected to use the summit to explore ways to expand engagement while managing long-standing differences over the border and regional security issues, the sources added.
Xi 's final travel plans and agenda for any potential bilateral between India and China are yet to be finalised , the sources said.
The Chinese foreign ministry said, "China attaches great importance to and actively participates in BRICS cooperation, and supports India , the current chair, in successfully hosting this year's BRICS summit."
"We currently have no information available to provide" about Xi 's visit , it said. Xi missed the last BRICS summit in 2025 in Brazil.
India 's foreign ministry did not comment.

INDIA -CHINA BORDER ISSUE The world's two most populous nations, both nuclear powers, share a roughly 3,800km, largely undemarcated and disputed border in the Himalayas.
Decades of relative peace along the border were shattered by 2020 clashes where 20 India n and four Chinese soldiers were killed. The incident led to a four-year military standoff before reaching a disengagement pact in October 2024.
But on Aug 12, India said peace along the border was critical to ties after reports that India n and Chinese army patrols came face-to-face in late July near a remote border.
India 's National Security Advisor Ajit Doval on Monday (Aug 24) started his visit to Beijing to meet Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi to hold talks on the boundary issue.
While India and China remain competitors, US President Donald Trump's trade policies have created one area of convergence, making Xi 's attendance a signal that neither side wants external pressure to undermine BRICS.

items.title: LinkedIn Users Are Rewriting the Past to Land Jobs
items.summary:
Researchers at Stanford University and Revelio Labs found that nearly 20% of established US LinkedIn users edited the descriptions or titles of jobs they had left years earlier, with tech workers doing so at a rate of nearly one in three.
These changes, dubbed "time travel," aren't made while memories are still fresh, but instead reflect a change in personal branding, with the median time-travel edit occurring more than four years after the user left the role. Beth Kowitt, Bloomberg Opinion Columnist covering corporate America joined Bloomberg Intelligence to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: メキシコが2年ぶりにサムライ債の発行計画、最大6本－関係者
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： メキシコは今週、2024年以来2年ぶりとなるサムライ債の発行を計画している。事情に詳しい関係者が明らかにした。

関係者によると、メキシコは年限3.5－20年の円建て債を最大6本発行する方向で調整している。28日に条件決定を予定しており、需要や市場環境によっては一部の年限の発行を見送る可能性がある。債券の初期価格交渉では、年限に応じてTONARミッドスワップに100－200ベーシスポイント（bp、1bp＝0.01%）上乗せした水準になる見通しだという。

メキシコ政府が前回サムライ債を発行したのは2024年8月で、5本発行し計1522億円を調達した。メキシコは1年半－2年おきにサムライ債を発行しており、今回もこれまでの発行ペースに沿ったものとなる。

メキシコの信用格付けには下押し圧力がかかっている。S&Pグローバル・レーティングは5月、財政状況の低迷が長引いていることや債務水準の上昇、経済成長の弱さを理由に、メキシコの格付け見通しを「ネガティブ」に変更した。ムーディーズ・レーティングスも5月に同様の懸念を示し、メキシコの格付けを投資適格級で最低の水準に引き下げた。国営のメキシコ石油公社（ペメックス）への継続的な支援が、政府の債務抑制能力を制約しているとしている。

メキシコは通商面でも不安定な状況にある。米国は7月、カナダ、メキシコとの米国・メキシコ・カナダ協定（USMCA）を更新せず、代わりに毎年見直す方針を示した。

その後、米国とカナダの交渉は21日に決裂した。合意案の文言が、カナダ側が合意したと認識していた内容と食い違う点が複数あったためだ。このため、メキシコと米国の協議の行方にも懸念が生じている。

items.title: Haiti gang raid leaves 47 dead, as residents demand stronger protections
items.author: Harold Isaac, Ives Surin
items.creator: Harold Isaac, Ives Surin
items.summary: At least 47 people were killed and 22 more injured in an overnight gang raid on a neighborhood overlooking Haiti's capital of Port-au-Prince, the U.N. said on Monday, prompting anger over the lack of protection from repeated deadly attacks.
items.body:
At least 47 people were killed and 22 more injured in an overnight gang raid on a neighborhood overlooking Haiti's capital of Port-au-Prince, the U.N. said on Monday, prompting anger over the lack of protection from repeated deadly attacks.
The United Nations Integrated Office in Haiti said estimates could still change.
The hillside community of Kenscoff, in a strategic position overlooking routes into the capital, has suffered a dozen attacks by armed gangs since last year, forcing thousands to flee their homes.
Powerful gangs under a broad alliance have for years cemented their influence over Haiti's capital and expanded to nearby regions, despite attempts by foreign nations to reinforce the country's outgunned police.
Haitian rights group RNDDH estimated 30 to 40 people were killed and 15 to 20 wounded in the raid, which began around 10:30 p.m. local time, but said it was difficult to assess a complete tally.
Even as Haiti's government decried a "heinous attack" and promised to reinforce security, residents demanded the local police chief step down, saying officers failed to protect people killed just minutes from the police station.
"Kenscoff will not be abandoned," the prime minister's office said on social media. "The government's authority will be restored, without weakness and without delay."
FORCED TO FLEE KENSCOFF Attacks in Kenscoff over two months in early 2025 saw more than 260 people killed and 200 homes destroyed or set on fire, forcing 3,000 people to flee, according to U.N. estimates.
Nearly a dozen more attacks have taken place since, including rapes, kidnapping, arson and livestock theft.
"My family are victims," said Coriolan Kendy, standing by his cousin's body, lying on the road in a blood-stained sheet. "People in Kenscoff are suffering and the government is to blame."
Another resident, Orisme, who did not share his last name, pleaded for the prime minister's support. "We live in humiliation and they do nothing for us," he said.
Some residents said several dozen police had tried to rebuff the armed men during the night, and some were injured. They added that they did not identify gang members among the dead.
Local media said several houses were set on fire, including the home of Jean William Pape, a leading public health expert.
"The police never gave up," national police chief Vladimir Paraison told reporters during a visit to Kenscoff later in the day.
Kenscoff overlooks routes into Petion-Ville — home to several embassies, upscale hotels and the temporary seat of government — as well as a major road from the capital into southern Haiti.
The violence may deepen concerns over Haiti's ability to [USN:S0N41D00K TEXT:"hold an election"] in December, its first in a decade. Successive governments have repeatedly postponed elections as armed gangs have expanded their influence.
The U.N.-backed Gang Suppression Force, which is mandated to help police fight gangs, aims to reach a capacity of more than 5,500 troops this autumn.
A spokesperson did not immediately respond to questions on whether the troops were reinforcing Kenscoff security.

items.title: ‘Their word is not their bond,’ policy expert slams last minute U.S. trade demands
items.author: Anam Khan
items.summary: Canada was right to impose counter-tariffs after the U.S. threatened its national sovereignty during trade talks, says a public policy expert.
items.body: Canada was right to impose counter-tariffs after the U.S. threatened its national sovereignty during trade talks, says a public policy expert. The U.S. crossed the line by introducing issues that were “thrown in at the last minute,” which include higher tariffs for trucks, an attempt to restrict free trade deals with other nations, and an attempt to control content regulation in Canada, Drew Fagan, a professor at the Munk School of Global Affairs and Public Policy at the University of Toronto, told BNN Bloomberg. “That’s extraordinarily sensitive,” he says. With the U.S. breaking its word even after Canada made painful concessions to secure a deal, Fagan says Prime Minister Mark Carney may feel “he has no choice but to introduce counter-tariffs.” Canada walked away from trade talks on Friday night after negotiations with the U.S. collapsed saying the U.S. “asked too much and they offered too little.” A 50 per cent tariff is now active on roughly $28 billion worth of goods. Carney vowed “Canada will match Washington’s new tariffs dollar for dollar in order to protect Canadian workers, farmers, families, and businesses.” On Monday, U.S. President Donald Trump threatened to further escalate the trade war by increasing tariffs on Canadian auto, car parts and steel by 50 per cent on Jan. 1, 2027. Fagan says he hopes the dispute freezes at the current level of tariffs and counter-tariffs instead of escalating into a tit-for-tat war because, ultimately, it is Canada that hurts the most. “Canada’s not a small economy. It’s a medium-sized economy. But up against a super heavyweight, frankly, both tariffs and counter tariffs hurt Canada more than they do the U.S.,” says Fagan. “Let’s hope that politically, the Trump administration is hurt by this.” ‘Signature was written in pencil’ meaning On Friday, Carney stated the Canadian government understood that the U.S. would put “a series of tariffs on its closest allies and use economic integration as a weapon. That its signature was written in pencil.” Fagan says after seeing the deals the U.S. struck with other countries, and watching new demands come in at the last minute when Canada thought it was close to a deal, it is becoming clear what Carney meant. “Their word is not their bond,” says Fagan. He says unlike Japan, South Korea and the U.K., which accepted U.S. terms, Canada’s economy is too deeply integrated with the U.S. to blindly accept a deal. “So we’re learning from others, in effect, and that’s what he meant by written in pencil. Also, the fact that there were new demands at the last second when we thought we were close to a deal, a painful deal, a very painful deal, on Tuesday,” says Fagan. He says the U.S. is even trying to push Canada to give up its independence in making trade deals with other countries, particularly China. “That also was a bright line,” says Fagan. ‘The fight is really with China’ On Sunday, Trump wrote “Canada wants the benefits of being a State, without being one!!” on his Truth Social account. Fagan explains that much of Trump’s understanding about bilateral relations is false. “The comments that his officials have made with regard to the Canada-U.S. relationship are almost apologetic,” says Fagan. “They don’t have a rationale for why they engaged in this offensive on trade terms, purely trade terms, given the depth of Canada-U.S. relations.” He says “the fight is really with China,” because the rise of China in global trade hurts manufacturing workers in both the U.S. and Canada, but the U.S. went after Canada instead. “The Western world, you could argue, made a strategic mistake with regard to the integration of China into the World Trade Organization and global trading,” says Fagan. “We should be an ally with the U.S. with regard to the issues that are on the table, as opposed to what we’ve been turned into by the Trump administration, which is a competitor.”

items.title: EXCLUSIVE Japan eyes tax breaks for non-core business sales in governance reform push, sources say
items.author: Makiko Yamazaki, Miho Uranaka
items.creator: Makiko Yamazaki, Miho Uranaka
items.summary: Japan's government is considering tax breaks on gains from sales of non-core businesses, a move that could accelerate long-delayed corporate restructuring and spur industry consolidation, two people with knowledge of the matter said.
items.body:
Japan's government is considering tax breaks on gains from sales of non-core businesses, a move that could accelerate long-delayed corporate restructuring and spur industry consolidation, two people with knowledge of the matter said.
The plan would remove a major obstacle to companies shedding non-core businesses and redeploying capital into growth areas, in what could become one of Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's most significant initiatives to advance corporate governance reform.
Under the plan, roughly 30% corporate tax on gains from sales of non-core businesses would be deferred indefinitely, provided companies reinvest the proceeds within several years in acquisitions aligned with their core operations and commit to investing in those businesses, one of the sources said.
The proposal is expected to be submitted as part of tax reform requests due at the end of this month, with details to be worked out before a final tax reform package for the next fiscal year is approved at year-end, said one of the sources, who declined to be identified as the matter is still private.
POOR CAPITAL ALLOCATION The initiative is modelled on Germany's tax reform in the early 2000s, which largely exempted corporations from taxes on gains from share disposals, helping dismantle the country's dense network of cross-shareholdings and making it easier for companies to reshape their business portfolios.
Non-core businesses often remain trapped within sprawling Japanese conglomerates because gains from divestitures are taxed, reducing the incentive to transfer assets to owners better positioned to extract value from them.
The result is often inefficient capital allocation. A recent government study found that about 65% of Japanese companies' invested capital remains tied up in businesses that fail to earn their cost of capital, largely offsetting value created by higher-performing units.
Such capital trapped in low-return operations is seen as limiting growth investment and weighing on long-term corporate value.
Japan has already introduced a range of measures to promote business overhauls over the years, including spin-off tax rules in 2017 and a partial spin-off regime in 2023, but business divestitures taking advantage of those rules have remained relatively limited.
A 2020 industry ministry report showed Japanese companies often lack clear divestment criteria and have traditionally prioritised maintaining group size, employment and corporate stability over portfolio reshaping.
The tax reform, if implemented, is likely to boost already sizzling M&A activity in Japan.
Deal activity involving Japanese companies last year more than doubled from the previous year to a record $353 billion, according to LSEG. Divestitures of Japanese businesses accounted for $44.7 billion of that total.

The plan would remove a major obstacle to companies shedding non-core businesses and redeploying capital into growth areas, in what could become one of Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's most significant initiatives to advance corporate governance reform.
Under the plan, roughly 30 per cent corporate tax on gains from sales of non-core businesses would be deferred indefinitely, provided companies reinvest the proceeds within several years in acquisitions aligned with their core operations and commit to investing in those businesses, one of the sources said.
The proposal is expected to be submitted as part of tax reform requests due at the end of this month, with details to be worked out before a final tax reform package for the next fiscal year is approved at year-end, said one of the sources, who declined to be identified as the matter is still private.

POOR CAPITAL ALLOCATION
The initiative is modelled on Germany's tax reform in the early 2000s, which largely exempted corporations from taxes on gains from share disposals, helping dismantle the country's dense network of cross-shareholdings and making it easier for companies to reshape their business portfolios.
Non-core businesses often remain trapped within sprawling Japanese conglomerates because gains from divestitures are taxed, reducing the incentive to transfer assets to owners better positioned to extract value from them.
The result is often inefficient capital allocation. A recent government study found that about 65 per cent of Japanese companies' invested capital remains tied up in businesses that fail to earn their cost of capital, largely offsetting value created by higher-performing units.
Such capital trapped in low-return operations is seen as limiting growth investment and weighing on long-term corporate value.
Japan has already introduced a range of measures to promote business overhauls over the years, including spin-off tax rules in 2017 and a partial spin-off regime in 2023, but business divestitures taking advantage of those rules have remained relatively limited.
A 2020 industry ministry report showed Japanese companies often lack clear divestment criteria and have traditionally prioritised maintaining group size, employment and corporate stability over portfolio reshaping.
The tax reform, if implemented, is likely to boost already sizzling M&A activity in Japan.
Deal activity involving Japanese companies last year more than doubled from the previous year to a record $353 billion, according to LSEG. Divestitures of Japanese businesses accounted for $44.7 billion of that total.

items.title: 米国が中国製品に7.5%関税へ、過剰生産能力で－米中首脳会談前に
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米国は中国の過剰生産能力を問題視し、中国製品に対して7.5%の関税を課す見通しだ。事情に詳しい複数の関係者が明らかにしたもので、来月予定されるトランプ米大統領と中国の習近平国家主席との会談を前に導入する方向だ。

今回の措置により、トランプ政権2期目に導入される対中関税は約20%に戻ることになる。中国政府はこれまで、同水準は米国との貿易休戦の合意内容に沿うものだとしてきた。これとは別に、トランプ政権1期目に導入され、バイデン政権下でも継続された関税も課されている。

最高裁判所は2月、中国を含む数十の国・地域からの輸入品に対するトランプ氏の関税を無効とした。今回の措置は、その後に保護主義的な通商政策を復活させる新たな一歩となる。一方、中国との貿易摩擦が合意済みの上限を超えて激化することは避ける。

匿名を条件に語った関係者によれば、具体的な税率は最終決定されたわけではない。トランプ氏は通商政策の発表に関し、最終段階で新たな要求を突き付ける、あるいは内容を変更するといった手法を採ることで知られる。

検討されている案の一つは、より高い対中関税率を発表した上で、その適用を一部停止し、実効税率を7.5%にするものだという。

どの税率をどの程度の期間、適用停止とするか、詳細はなお協議中だと関係者は語った。米中は、11月10日に期限を迎える1年間の休戦を定めた、いわゆる貿易協定の延長も模索しているという。

トランプ政権は今年3月、過剰生産能力を巡る懸念を理由に、1974年通商法301条に基づき、主要な貿易相手国・地域を対象に調査を開始した。

政権当局者は、トランプ氏と習氏が9月24日に首都ワシントンで会談する予定を前に、過剰生産能力に関する調査結果を公表したい考えだ。事情に詳しい関係者によると、過剰生産能力に関する報告書の詳細は法的に難しい問題を伴っている。

米通商代表部（USTR）のグリア代表は7月、ブルームバーグテレビジョンに対し、過剰生産能力に関する調査は複雑なため、強制労働を巡る別の調査より時間がかかると述べた。また、調査の遅れは中国との休戦を維持する取り組みとは無関係だと説明した。

items.title: 【米国市況】S&P500反落、半導体株に売り－円は小幅安で159円10銭台
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 24日の米株式市場でS&P500種株価指数は反落した。原油安というプラス材料を、半導体株の下げが打ち消した格好となった。ベッセント米財務長官がイランを世界経済から孤立させる計画を打ち出したことを受け、その中身を見極めたいとのムードが広がった。

フィラデルフィア半導体株指数は一時、前週末比4.1%下落した。米半導体大手エヌビディアが26日に発表する決算では、同社が圧倒的な優位を維持していることがあらためて示される見通し。しかし、エヌビディア株はこれで7営業日続落と、2022年以来の長期下落局面となった。

エヌビディアの大口顧客の一部は、AI半導体を搭載したサーバーを値上げするとの通知を受けた。週末のこの報道を受け、メモリー領域に特化した上場投資信託（ETF）は5.9%安で引けた。ナスダック100指数は1%安で終えた。

ベッセント氏は記者会見で、「われわれは世界各地に広がるイランの金融ネットワークに対し、経済的な猛攻撃を開始する」と表明。「イラン政権を経済的に窒息させるものだ」とし、イラン資金の洗浄に関与する場合、ドルへのアクセスを遮断すると述べた。

モルガン・スタンレー傘下Eトレード・ファイナンシャルのクリス・ラーキン氏は「米国による対イラン経済制裁の詳細や、米財務省による長期金利引き下げの取り組み、そして経済データが市場心理を大きく左右する可能性がある」と述べた。「エヌビディアをはじめとするハイテク企業の決算が、相場の勢いに大きな影響を与えそうだ」とも語った。

市場関係者は、ウォーシュ米連邦準備制度理事会（FRB）議長が28日にワイオミング州ジャクソンホールで講演を行う際、根強いインフレにFRBがどう対応すべきかについて、自身の見解を明確にすることにも期待している。

クエスター・キャピタル・パートナーズのリチャード・ライル氏は「米財務省が先週、債券市場で異例の措置に踏み切ったことで、ウォーシュ議長は難しい立場に置かれている。積極的な情報発信を好まないようにみえる議長にとっては、なおさらだ」と述べた。

items.title: 9月の相次ぐ社債発行、消化への懸念は行き過ぎ－JPモルガン
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 投資適格級社債市場では、9月に社債発行が相次ぐ見通しだ。JPモルガン・アセット・マネジメントのポートフォリオマネジャー、ケルシー・ベロ氏は、ブルームバーグテレビジョンとのインタビューで、社債への旺盛な需要を踏まえれば、大量発行への懸念は行き過ぎの可能性があるとの見方を示した。

ベロ氏によると、9月の発行額については、1750億－2500億ドル（約27兆8400億－39兆7700億円）と幅広い予想が出ている。クレジットのポートフォリオマネジャーからは、発行額が2500億ドルに達しても「実際にはそれほど問題ではない」との声が聞かれるという。ただ、ベロ氏は、最終的な発行額を巡る不確実性が、市場関係者にとって事前の対応を難しくしていると指摘した。

市場では予想のばらつき自体が緊張の要因となっている。発行額予想の下限と上限には750億ドルの開きがあり、例年、社債発行が最も活発になる月の一つである9月を前に、ポートフォリオマネジャーはポジションを取りにくくなっている。

AIインフラ整備への支出を賄うため企業の借り入れが膨らむ中、社債発行は過去最速のペースが続いている。米国の優良企業による社債発行額は8月、3カ月連続で月間最高を更新した。

借り入れ急増の影響が表れる中、投資家は購入する債券やその価格を以前より厳しく選別するようになっている。データセンター事業の資金調達を目指す企業の中には、投資適格級の債券であっても、数十億ドルを調達するためにジャンク債投資家への依存を強めるところも出ている。

8月の社債発行額はすでに1570億ドルに達した。アルファベットによる250億ドルの起債に加え、アッヴィやアドバンスト・マイクロ・デバイセズ（AMD）による大型案件が発行額を押し上げた。

ベロ氏は「記録的な供給がある一方、需要も過去最高となっている」と述べた。こうした需給関係により、9月の大量発行は懸念されるほど大きな問題にはならない可能性があるという。

items.title: 米国、対イラン追加制裁を発表へ－財務長官「経済的生命線全て断つ」
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： ベッセント米財務長官は24日、イランに対する新たな経済制裁措置を発表する見通しだ。約6カ月に及ぶ戦争の終結を目指し、米政府は軍事攻撃の威嚇から、徹底した経済制裁による圧力強化へと軸足を移す。

ベッセント氏は予定している会見で、イランを一段と効果的に孤立させる計画の詳細を明らかにする。米国は数十年にわたり広範な対イラン制裁を科してきたが、今回さらに強化する。具体的な内容は不明だが、中国やトルコ、インドなどイランの主要貿易相手国の一部に影響が及ぶ可能性がある。

アラブ首長国連邦（UAE）は先週、イランとの経済関係を全て断絶したと発表。湾岸の米同盟国によるこうした動きが、ワシントンの戦略を後押ししている。

ベッセント氏は英紙フィナンシャル・タイムズ（FT）への寄稿で、「世界は、イランが孤立するまで、この圧政政権を支えるあらゆる経済的生命線を断つことがわれわれの目的だと理解すべきだ」と述べた。

イラン経済は既に極めて厳しい状況にあり、米海軍による海上封鎖で重要な原油輸出が大幅に制限されている。

イランでは年間インフレ率が80％を超え、人口9000万人の国民への圧力が一段と強まっている。イラン通貨リアルは対ドルで過去最安値に沈む。トランプ米大統領が先週、イランへの経済圧力を強める計画を明らかにして以降、4.5％下落した。

イランはこれまでも制裁をしのいできた経緯があり、米国の今回の措置が新たな軍事攻撃を招く恐れもある。イランは、米国の制裁計画を支援する国には報復すると警告した。2月下旬の戦争開始以降、イランは湾岸の米同盟国に数千発のミサイルやドローンを撃ち込んでいる。

イラン最高安全保障委員会のレザイ事務局長は23日夜、「米国によるイラン国民への経済戦争に参加したり、これを支援したりする国の行為を戦争行為とみなす」とXへの投稿で表明。

その上で、「ホルムズ海峡からも、ペルシャ湾のどこからも、原油は一滴たりとも輸出されなくなる」と述べた。

items.title: As US border reopens to Mexican cattle, concerns persist over screwworm spread
items.author: Cassandra Garrison, Leah Douglas
items.creator: Cassandra Garrison, Leah Douglas
items.summary: Mexico is bolstering its screwworm containment campaign in northern border states where recent cases have been detected, heightening scrutiny of livestock exports as cross-border trade resumed on Monday under a phased U.S. reopening.
items.body:
Mexico is bolstering its screwworm containment campaign in northern border states where recent cases have been detected, heightening scrutiny of livestock exports as cross-border trade resumed on Monday under a phased U.S. reopening.
The reopening marks the first easing of a U.S. ban imposed more than a year ago to keep out the flesh-eating pest, as imports [USN:FWN43Q0OT TEXT:"resumed"] initially through Arizona .
The plan has drawn criticism from some U.S. cattle groups and state officials who argue that resuming imports could increase screwworm risks even as the parasite continues to spread in northern Mexico and has already been detected in Texas and New Mexico.
Mexican Agriculture Minister Columba Lopez said authorities would reinforce the dispersal of sterile flies in Sonora and Chihuahua, a key eradication strategy aimed at preventing the parasite from reproducing.
Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins told reporters on Monday that the USDA feels it has "taken every step to protect the American (cattle) herd and the American consumer, and so now we can slowly begin to reopen the ports."
The USDA plans to open two more New Mexico ports, one in 30 days and another in 60 days, Rollins said. "We don't plan to open any Texas ports anytime soon just because that is where the real activity is," Rollins said.
The USDA has identified 46 cases of screwworm in New Mexico and Texas, with two currently active, according to the agency's website.
NEW CASES IN MEXICO A USDA website on Monday said it reopened the Douglas, Arizona, port to cattle imports from Mexico "guided by overlapping safeguards and a science-based import protocol" agreed upon by the two countries. The USDA will next evaluate the reopening of ports in Santa Teresa and Columbus, New Mexico, to cattle, bison, and horses.
"The opening of ports may be paused if USDA identifies increased risk in Sonora or Chihuahua via post-opening audits or other observations/information," the site said.
The reopening will begin with exports of 700 head of cattle per day during the first week, increasing to 900 per day in the second week and gradually rising to around 1,300 per day, according to Mexico’s National Confederation of Livestock Organizations (CNOG).
If additional Chihuahua border crossings are reopened in the fourth quarter, Mexico could export up to 200,000 head of cattle in 2026, with an estimated value of about $420 million at U.S. market prices, CNOG said. Its base scenario for 2027 projects exports of 1.09 million head of cattle, valued at roughly $2.1 billion in the U.S. market.
Chihuahua, one of Mexico's most important cattle-exporting states, has reported 183 confirmed screwworm cases since detecting its first case in July, while neighboring Sonora state has reported two confirmed cases after announcing its first detection last week. Sonora has activated emergency surveillance and containment protocols, while Chihuahua has intensified inspections, livestock movement controls and treatment campaigns to prevent further spread.
The sterile insect technique works by releasing millions of sterilized screwworm flies that mate with wild females but produce no offspring, gradually driving down the pest population. Mexico recently opened a sterile-fly production plant in Chiapas, while the U.S. is building its own production facility in Texas, expected to be completed by the [USN:L6N4470WS TEXT:"spring of 2027"].
Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum referred to the sterile-fly technique as a "modern" and "effective" way to fight screwworm.
"That allows us to open the border," Sheinbaum said in her daily press conference.

items.title: A medida que la frontera de EEUU vuelve a abrirse al ganado mexicano, persiste preocupación por propagación del gusano barrenador
items.author: Cassandra Garrison, Leah Douglas
items.creator: Cassandra Garrison, Leah Douglas
items.summary: México está reforzando su campaña de contención de la mosca del gusano barrenador en los estados fronterizos del norte, donde se han detectado casos recientes, lo que ha intensificado los controles sobre las exportaciones de ganado tras la reanudación del comercio transfronterizo el lunes, en el marco de la reapertura gradual de Estados Unidos.
items.body:
México está reforzando su campaña de contención de la mosca del gusano barrenador en los estados fronterizos del norte, donde se han detectado casos recientes, lo que ha intensificado los controles sobre las exportaciones de ganado tras la reanudación del comercio transfronterizo el lunes, en el marco de la reapertura gradual de Estados Unidos.
La reapertura supone la primera flexibilización de la prohibición impuesta por Estados Unidos hace más de un año para impedir la entrada de esta plaga carnívora, ya que las importaciones se reanudaron inicialmente a través de Arizona.
El plan ha suscitado críticas por parte de algunas asociaciones ganaderas estadounidenses y de autoridades estatales, que argumentan que la reanudación de las importaciones podría aumentar el riesgo de infestación por el gusano barrenador, en un momento en que el parásito sigue propagándose por el norte de México y ya se ha detectado en Texas y Nuevo México.
La secretaria de Agricultura de México, Columba López, afirmó que las autoridades reforzarían la liberación de moscas estériles en Sonora y Chihuahua, una estrategia clave de erradicación destinada a impedir que el parásito se reproduzca.
"Vamos a mantener nosotros todo el sistema de trazabilidad desde la nacencia hasta que coloquemos el ganado del otro lado", dijo López en un enlace desde Sonora a la conferencia de prensa matutina de la presidente Claudia Sheinbaum. "Y la otra parte es reforzar la dispersión de moscas (vamos a) mantener muchísimos controles de seguridad", añadió.
La secretaria de Agricultura de Estados Unidos, Brooke Rollins, dijo el lunes a periodistas que el Departamento de Agricultura de Estados Unidos (USDA por su sigla en inglés) considera que ha "tomado todas las medidas necesarias para proteger el ganado estadounidense y al consumidor estadounidense, por lo que ahora podemos empezar poco a poco a reabrir los puertos".
El USDA tiene previsto abrir dos puertos más en Nuevo México, uno dentro de 30 días y otro dentro de 60 días, indicó Rollins. "No tenemos previsto abrir ningún puerto de Texas a corto plazo, simplemente porque es allí donde se concentra la actividad real", afirmó.
NUEVOS CASOS EN MÉXICO El lunes, la página en internet del USDA informó de que se había reabierto el puerto de Douglas, en Arizona, a las importaciones de ganado procedente de México, "guiándose por medidas de seguridad complementarias y un protocolo de importación con base científica" acordado por ambos países. El USDA evaluará la reapertura de los puertos de Santa Teresa y Columbus, en Nuevo México, al ganado vacuno, los bisontes y los caballos.
"La apertura de los puertos podría suspenderse si el USDA detecta un aumento del riesgo en Sonora o Chihuahua a través de auditorías posteriores a la apertura u otras observaciones o información", indicó en el sitio.
La reapertura comenzará con exportaciones de 700 cabezas de ganado al día durante la primera semana, pasando a 900 al día en la segunda semana y aumentando gradualmente hasta alcanzar unas 1,300 al día, dijo la Confederación Nacional de Organizaciones Ganaderas (CNOG) de México en un comunicado.
Si se reabren más pasos fronterizos de Chihuahua en el cuarto trimestre, México podría exportar hasta 200,000 cabezas de ganado en 2026, con un valor estimado de unos 420 millones de dólares a precios del mercado estadounidense, según la CNOG. Su escenario base para 2027 prevé exportaciones de 1.09 millones de cabezas de ganado, valoradas en aproximadamente 2,100 millones de dólares en el mercado estadounidense.
Chihuahua, uno de los estados mexicanos más importantes en la exportación de ganado, ha notificado 183 casos confirmados de gusano barrenador desde que detectó su primer caso en julio, mientras que el vecino estado Sonora ha notificado dos casos confirmados tras anunciar su primera detección la semana pasada.
Sonora ha activado protocolos de vigilancia y contención de emergencia, mientras que Chihuahua ha intensificado las inspecciones, los controles de movimiento de ganado y las campañas de tratamiento para evitar una mayor propagación.
La técnica de insectos estériles consiste en liberar millones de moscas esterilizadas que se aparean con hembras silvestres pero no producen descendencia, lo que reduce gradualmente la población de la plaga. México ha inaugurado recientemente una planta de producción de moscas estériles en Chiapas, mientras que Estados Unidos está construyendo su propia instalación de producción en Texas, cuya finalización está prevista para la primavera de 2027.
La presidenta Sheinbaum se refirió a la técnica de la mosca estéril como una forma "moderna" y "eficaz" de combatir al gusano barrenador.
"Eso nos permite que se abra la frontera", afirmó la mandataria en su rueda de prensa.

items.title: 英国、ウクライナにミサイル部品の機密開示へ－防空能力強化を支援
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 英国のバーナム首相は24日、ウクライナを訪問し、ゼレンスキー大統領への支持を示すとともに、冬を前にウクライナの防空能力強化を支援する方針を表明した。同氏は、長距離巡航ミサイル「スカルプ」に使われる英国製部品に関する機密情報について、英防衛企業MBDAによる開示を認めると発表した。

バーナム氏はウクライナによるロシアへの抵抗を、第2次世界大戦での英国のナチス・ドイツとの戦いになぞらえ、結束を強調した。7月の首相就任以来、バーナム氏は国内政策を優先してきたが、国際舞台での指導力も強調したい考えだ。

ウクライナ独立35周年を記念し、キーウの聖ソフィア大聖堂前で行った演説で、バーナム氏は「ウクライナ国民の圧倒的な強さには、心から畏敬の念を抱く」と述べ、「20世紀にはわが国が欧州の自由の炎を守り続けた。21世紀にはあなた方がその炎を守っている。ロシアはわが国に言語道断の脅しをかけているが、われわれはウクライナへの支援を続ける」と呼びかけた。

バーナム氏は同日、ゼレンスキー氏と「有志連合」による会合も共同主催した。ドイツのメルツ首相やフランスのマクロン大統領がオンライン参加したとみられる。

スカルプは、英国の長距離巡航ミサイル「ストームシャドー」のフランス製造版で、両ミサイルには英仏共通の技術が使われている。情報開示により、フランスとウクライナは早ければ今年末にも、ウクライナ国内でスカルプを組み立てられるようになる。

ロシア大統領府のペスコフ報道官は24日、スカルプに使われる英国製部品の機密情報開示の計画について、ロシア政府は「極めて否定的」に受け止めていると記者団に述べた。ペスコフ氏は「英国はウクライナ政府側に立ってこの戦争に参加し、組織的かつ継続的に火に油を注ぎ、和平プロセスのいかなる進展も阻止しようと策を巡らせている」と語った。

同氏は、ロシア軍がこうしたミサイルの生産拠点の特定を進めており、「関連施設を破壊するための措置を講じている」としている。

items.title: トランプ氏、カナダ製自動車への関税倍増と表明－対立さらに激化
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： トランプ米大統領は、カナダから輸入する自動車・同部品に関する関税を来年から2倍に引き上げると表明した。両国の貿易紛争が一段と激化する。

トランプ氏は24日、「全ての自動車とトラック、大型・小型共に、および自動車部品、鉄鋼に対する関税率」を来年1月1日に50%に引き上げると、自身のSNS「トゥルース・ソーシャル」に投稿した。

自動車に対する関税率は現在25%で、このうち米国で生産された部品などの価値を除いた部分のみに適用されている。輸入鉄鋼には既に50%の関税が課されている。

米国とカナダの交渉は21日に決裂し、米国は多くのカナダ製品に対する関税率を50%に引き上げた。トランプ氏による今回の新たな警告は、対立に拍車を掛けるものだ。カナダのカーニー首相は、米国による関税と同額の報復関税を9月8日から課すと表明している。

自動車関税が実際に引き上げられれば、過去数十年にわたって緊密に一体化してきた米国とカナダのサプライチェーンに大きな混乱をもたらす可能性がある。

トランプ氏はこれまでにも自動車部品に関税を課す方針を示してきたが、実務面で複雑な作業を伴うことから実施には至っていなかった。

自動車に含まれる米国産部分を関税対象から除外する現行措置を、トランプ政権がどのように扱うのかは、現時点で明らかになっていない。この除外措置は実際の関税負担を大きく左右する。カナダから輸入される自動車は通常、半分を米国で生産するため、実際に課される関税率は表面上の税率の半分程度となっている。

トランプ氏が24日に発表した新たな関税が実際に発動されるかどうかも不透明だ。発動日を1月1日としたことで、交渉再開の余地が生まれる。ただ、カナダ側は11月の中間選挙までに交渉が再開する可能性は低いとみている。

カーニー氏は週末に発動された関税への対抗措置として、9月8日に独自の関税を発動する予定で、米国はカナダが実施すればさらに対抗措置を強化すると警告している。

items.title: Trump administration moves to impose over $100K fee on H-1B worker visas
items.author: Reuters
items.summary: A federal judge in June ruled that the fee was illegal and blocked the Trump administration from collecting it.
items.body: President Donald Trump's administration on Monday released a proposed regulation to codify an unprecedented more than $100,000 fee on new H-1B visas for highly skilled foreign workers that Trump first imposed last year but has been blocked by the courts. The fee first imposed by Trump in a temporary proclamation last year vastly raises the cost of the visas that are heavily relied on in the tech, education and research sectors. A federal judge in June ruled that the fee was illegal and blocked the Trump administration from collecting it. A Boston-based appeals court is reviewing that decision while a different court considers whether a judge in Washington, DC, properly rejected a challenge to the fee by a major business group. Trump's 2025 proclamation imposing the fee expires in September, one year after it was issued, but directed the US Department of Homeland Security to adopt regulations making it permanent. The proposed $103,265 fee by DHS, posted online in the Federal Register on Monday to be formally published on Tuesday, kicks off a 30-day public comment period. The rule could be finalized by the end of the year. The H-1B program allows U.S. employers to hire foreign workers with training in specialty fields and offers 65,000 visas annually, with another 20,000 for workers with advanced degrees, approved for three to six years. The order Trump issued last year sharply increased the cost of obtaining some H-1B visas, which had typically come with about $2,000 to $5,000 in fees, depending on various factors.   DEBATE OVER VISA PROGRAM  Trump, a Republican, and other critics of the H-1B program say it is abused by many companies who replace American workers with cheaper foreign labor. But business groups and many individual companies have said the visa program is needed to address a lack of qualified American workers for some jobs and to allow U.S. businesses to recruit top talent. About 70 employers had paid the $100,000 fee on a total of 85 visa applications as of late February, according to court filings.  In imposing the fee, Trump invoked the president's power under federal immigration law to restrict the entry of certain foreign nationals who would be detrimental to US interests. The fee is being challenged by the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, the largest US business lobbying group, Democratic-led states and a coalition of unions and employers. Those lawsuits could be amended to challenge the rule proposed this week once it is finalized. LEGAL CHALLENGES MOUNT  The lawsuits claim that Trump's power to restrict entry does not allow him to override the law that created the H-1B visa program. The states and groups that sued also say that the Homeland Security Department cannot impose fees, taxes or other means to generate revenue for the United States without permission from Congress.   The Trump administration has maintained that the fee is not a traditional tax and that courts have little power to question the president's authority to restrict entry into the country. Amid Trump's broader immigration crackdown, employers last year registered for about 344,000 H-1B visas, down more than 25% from 2024 and fewer than half of the 794,000 visas sought in 2023, according to data from U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services. The Trump administration has also ordered enhanced vetting of H-1B applicants and proposed a new visa selection process that would favor higher-skilled and better-paid workers.  Earlier in August, the Department of Homeland Security in a separate rule added fees of up to $4,500 to applications to extend the stay of H-1B workers or to transfer employees based in other countries to the United States.

items.title: Capricor's Duchenne drug gets three-month FDA extension after new data submission
items.author: Kamal Choudhury
items.creator: Kamal Choudhury
items.summary: Capricor Therapeutics said on Monday the U.S. Food and Drug Administration had extended the review period for its experimental cell therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy by three months.
items.body:
Capricor Therapeutics (CAPR.O) said on Monday the U.S. Food and Drug Administration had extended the review period for its experimental cell therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy by three months.
The delay follows Capricor's submission of new 24-month data from its late-stage study, along with extra analyses, to support a refined proposed indication focused on upper limb function, the trial's main goal.
The therapy, deramiocel, last year failed to get FDA's [USN:L4N3T80S4 TEXT:"approval"] to treat cardiomyopathy, or a heart muscle disease, in patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy. The regulator said the treatment did not meet efficacy requirements and asked for more data.
Earlier this year, Capricor resubmitted its application with new data, and was expecting a decision by August 22.
But last month, an FDA advisory panel [USN:L4N43V2DJ TEXT:"voted against"] the therapy's effectiveness data, while the [USN:L4N43T0YE TEXT:"agency staff flagged concerns"] about changes to how the company measured trial results.
Following this, Capricor Chief Executive Linda Marban said the company will submit an amendment with new data focused on improving upper limb muscle function.
The health regulator has accepted the amendment, citing the high unmet medical need for Duchenne patients, and classified the submission as a "major amendment" and set the new deadline to November 22, Capricor said.
Shares of the company rose 15% to $7.25.
Marbán said the additional follow-up data gives the company "one of the most extensive clinical datasets evaluating upper limb function in Duchenne," and that the trial had [USN:L4N3X90YA TEXT:"met its main goal"] with a statistically significant benefit.
Deramiocel is being developed to treat Duchenne, a rare genetic disease that affects about 15,000 people in the United States, primarily boys.
The key question remains whether the new data and analyses are sufficient to "address the FDA's concerns and support approval for the refined indication focused on upper limb function," said H.C. Wainwright analysts.
items.raw_description: Capricor Therapeutics said on Monday the U.S. Food and Drug Administration had extended the review period for its experimental cell therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy by three months.

Aug 24 : The U.S. Federal Trade Commission and a group of states settled with Zillow ahead of trial on Monday, ending claims the online real estate platform illegally paid Rocket Companies' Redfin $100 million to stop competing in apartment rental listings.
The FTC and five states were ready to argue at trial scheduled to start Monday that the Zillow-Redfin partnership drove up costs for landlords and decreased listing quality for renters. More than 30 per cent of Americans rent their homes, according to census data. 
Under the settlement, Redfin can continue to display Zillow ads on its sites but will resume its rental advertising business within six months, the FTC and states said.
While Democratic state attorneys general have clashed with the Trump administration on other matters, both the FTC and the states called the settlement a win.

New York Attorney General Letitia James said the lawsuit restored competition in online listing platforms, "critical tools that New Yorkers rely on to find affordable homes."
Virginia, Arizona, Connecticut and Washington were also plaintiffs.
FTC Chair Andrew Ferguson said the settlement will provide competition in rental markets that is "an integral component of President Donald Trump’s domestic housing agenda."
A Redfin spokesperson said the settlement allows the company to maintain its partnership with Zillow through at least 2030 while building its own rentals business.
Zillow rentals executive Michael Sherman said the settlement is positive and "enables us to keep our energy on innovating for renters and property managers."
ZILLOW-REDFIN PARTNERSHIP ALLEGEDLY RAISED AD PRICES
Zillow and Redfin made a deal in February 2025: Redfin would wind down its rental listing business, refer its customers to Zillow, and display copies of Zillow's listings on its site. Redfin agreed to stay out of the business for up to nine years.
In return, Zillow agreed to pay Redfin $100 million, plus fees for each renter who signaled interest in a property. 
The FTC sued the companies, as did New York, Virginia, Arizona, Connecticut and Washington. They said that before the deal, Zillow and Redfin were competing to list vacancies in buildings with more than 25 units. 
After Redfin stopped competing, Zillow customers paid an average of 14.5 per cent more per listing, an expert for the FTC and states estimated, while some property managers stopped buying online listings.
Zillow had said in court papers that the deal put more listings on both sites and helped it compete with market leader CoStar Group. Exclusive deals are common in the industry, Zillow had said.
